transcript.name: Anna Kovačević
transcript.text: Before we go any further, can we get specific? Last time, the handover failed and ownership was vague. If we don't fix that, it won't matter who leads this pitch. Can someone explain—who's actually accountable if things get complicated?

transcript.name: Lucía Mendoza
transcript.text: If I can add, maybe we should list out who’s taking which part, and who steps in if there’s a problem. That way, no one’s confused if things get tricky.

transcript.name: Élise Moreau
transcript.text: Maybe we should lay out all the main parts of the pitch on the board, then talk through who wants to own each section. That way, nobody gets left guessing if something changes or goes wrong. I’m happy to help map it out—does that work for everyone?

transcript.name: Wei Zhou
transcript.text: Maybe before we commit, could we run through a quick example where things get complicated? Just so we know if this plan covers it.

transcript.name: Todd Ramsey
transcript.text: I think having clear owners and backups for each piece is the way to go. I’m fine to handle the technical systems part, and I’ll make sure my team’s covered if something comes up. Just want to avoid the confusion we had last time.

transcript.name: Erik Lundström
transcript.text: I think É lise’s idea makes sense. If we write out each part and who’s on it, it’ll help. But maybe we also add a backup for each section, just in case someone’s out or overloaded?

transcript.name: Lilian Njoroge
transcript.text: I think it helps to list out responsibilities and backups, but maybe we still need to pick one person who’s ultimately responsible if something goes off track. Otherwise, we might end up in the same situation as before.

transcript.name: Marcus Webb
transcript.text: Alright, let’s stop splitting hairs. I’ll lead the pitch, period. Lucia, you handle client strategy—Élise, keep the board updated. Todd, tech. Everyone heard? If there’s a problem, it’s on me. Any objections, say it now, or we’re done debating.

transcript.name: Trang Nguyen
transcript.text: Okay, so just to double-check—if Marcus is out for any reason, who covers? Maybe we should write backup names next to each part, just so it’s all clear?

transcript.name: Amitesh Iyer
transcript.text: Just to check, are we actually noting down backups for each part now? That’ll keep things clear if someone’s out. I can help list them out if needed.

transcript.name: Marcus Webb
transcript.text: Alright, Amitesh—yes, write the backup for each part right on the board. If I’m out, Lucia steps up. For tech, if Todd’s out, Erik covers. Same logic everywhere. Let’s get it on paper and stop circling.

transcript.name: Trang Nguyen
transcript.text: Alright, I’ve got that—Erik’s my backup for data flow, right? Just checking so nothing slips through.

transcript.name: Todd Ramsey
transcript.text: Alright, I’ve got Erik listed as my backup for tech. If anything changes, just let me know. Otherwise, I’ll get started on the system docs update.

transcript.name: Amitesh Iyer
transcript.text: Alright, I've got my section and backup written down. If anything changes, just loop me in. Otherwise, I’m good with this setup.

transcript.name: Élise Moreau
transcript.text: All clear from my side. I’ll keep the board updated—let me know if anything changes. Otherwise, I think we’re set.

transcript.name: Lilian Njoroge
transcript.text: All clear on my side too. If anything changes for my section, just let me know.

transcript.name: Wei Zhou
transcript.text: Just to confirm, I’m listed as backup for compliance and documentation, right? If so, that’s fine with me. If anything changes, just let me know.

transcript.name: Anna Kovačević
transcript.text: Before we finish—does anyone see a gap in what’s written down? If you’re unsure about anything, now’s the time to flag it. Better to pause here than miss something obvious.

transcript.name: Erik Lundström
transcript.text: Nothing jumps out to me as missing, but if anyone’s got doubts, now’s the time. Better to say it than keep quiet.

transcript.name: Lucía Mendoza
transcript.text: Nothing seems missing to me, but if anyone’s unsure or wants to double-check their part, now’s a good time. It’s better to speak up than wonder later.

transcript.name: Todd Ramsey
transcript.text: Just checking—are we good on timing between sections? Last time things slipped because one part held up another. If anyone's got concerns, better to say it now.

transcript.name: Lucía Mendoza
transcript.text: On timing—do we all feel clear about when each part needs to be handed over? If anyone’s unsure, maybe we can just go through it quickly.

transcript.name: Lilian Njoroge
transcript.text: Could we just run through the handover timings quickly? I want to be sure I’m clear on when my section’s expected, so there’s no mix-up later.

transcript.name: Erik Lundström
transcript.text: Probably best if we just run through each section’s timing out loud, one by one. That way no one’s left guessing.

transcript.name: Wei Zhou
transcript.text: For my section—compliance and documentation—can we just confirm the exact handover time? I want to be sure I’ve got it right. Thanks.

transcript.name: Anna Kovačević
transcript.text: Let’s just go section by section—say the handover time for each out loud, right now. If anyone’s not clear, speak up. I’d rather catch a mix-up here than next week.

transcript.name: Marcus Webb
transcript.text: Okay, we’re not leaving until every section’s handover time is said out loud. One shot—when is your piece done and who’s it going to? If you’re not clear, say it now. No excuses later.

transcript.name: Élise Moreau
transcript.text: For my piece, I’ll have the design handover done by Wednesday noon, and I’ll pass it directly to Todd. If anything slips, I’ll flag it right away. Anyone not clear on theirs?

transcript.name: Amitesh Iyer
transcript.text: For my part, I’ll have the backend update done by Thursday morning and I’ll pass it straight to Lucía. If there’s any delay, I’ll message right away. Anyone see a clash with that?
